messages:
sam: Heads-up: I posted an RFC draft for a Tiered Finalization Service (TFS) to handle provisional->final billing event convergence. Goal: reduce noisy backfills and give auditable final events.
anya: quick q - how is TFS different from the LAM/backfill approach we've talked about before?
sam: TL;DR: two-tier finalization. micro-finalizer for low-volume fingerprints (fast, <30s), and convergent finalizer for high-volume where we use a merge window (configurable, default 3m) and associative merge functions. Both emit the same canonical event shape.
li: makes sense. micro-finalizer sits close to ingest? any perf impact?
sam: micro-finalizer runs as a nearline service reading staging topic and writing canonical immediately with conservative heuristics. Convergent finalizer batches small windows to ensure deterministic merges. Neither is in the sync request path; ingest still writes provisional event synchronously.
anya: where do we keep provenance for audits/backfills? full payloads in hot store are expensive.
sam: raw provisional events -> cold S3 (90d). TFS materializes a lightweight provenance record in the audit DB (fingerprint, input_ids, blob_hashes, chosen_version) kept 30d. We log a compact human-readable audit entry for every finalized event.
li: failure/replay story? if merge logic changes, how do we correct canonical stream?
sam: we support deterministic reprocess: re-run TFS over raw blobs for a partition and emit a replacement canonical segment + tombstone manifest. Consumers subscribe to patch topics for applying diffs. We'll gate large replays behind a replay-quarantine and rate limits.
ops-bot: NOTE: replay-quarantine enabled by default. Large replays will auto-escalate to oncall.
sre-robo: ops question - kafka vs storage for exactly-once?
li: prefer deterministic commit keys + idempotent producer. Format example:
```
commit_key = f"{fingerprint}|{window_start_iso}|{shard_id}"
```
If identical commit_key seen, drop duplicate. Also write a WAL marker before emitting to canonical topic.
anya: cross-region? tenant events may land in multiple regions. Centralize TFS or run per-region shards?
sam: plan: shard TFS by billing-partition (consistent hashing) and run a lightweight forwarder in each region that ships provisional events to owning partition. That reduces cross-region consensus complexity. Audit record includes source_region.
li: API surface - do we expose provisional vs finalized values? customers worry about surprise adjustments.
sam: yes - API returns provisional immediately with "provisional_id" and a link to audit record. Finalized amounts appear after finalization; adjustments come as delta events with audit links. Console shows both with lineage.
anya: SLOs and alerts? what triggers ops attention?
sam: dashboards: pending_per_partition, avg_finalization_latency, mismatch_ratio (provisional vs finalized). Alerts when mismatch_ratio > 2% or reprocess rate high.
li: rollout plan?
sam: staged: 1) shadow mode in staging (TFS emits canonical but consumers still read provisional) - 2w. 2) internal canary (analytics & platform teams) - 1w. 3) parallel billing run 72h, diff checks, then cutover - 1w. Owners: design (sam), infra/shard routing (li), audit store (anya).
ops-bot: TODO created: TFS-shadow-run scheduled.
sam: I'll post RFC link and state diagram later today. If no blockers I'll open infra tickets tomorrow.
anya: +1
li: +1
sre-robo: +1
